name: trigger_guard
comment: ADR-0042: a trigger step as data — the declaration rendered through the dialect (drop, then create) — and the MIG-012 guard reused for triggers: a change step declares the expected previous declaration (expectTrigger); a trigger rewritten outside the code refuses with MIG-012 (the atomic run leaves the hand-written one untouched); force recreates from the code. The deep expect reads the live trigger back as its declaration.

up: create table widgets (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, log TEXT) STRICT

trigger.sql: update widgets set log = 'v1' where id in (select n.id from {new: id} n);

expectTrigger.sql: update widgets set log = 'v1' where id in (select n.id from {new: id} n);

trigger.sql: update widgets set log = 'v2' where id in (select n.id from {new: id} n);

up: create table widgets (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, log TEXT) STRICT

trigger.sql: update widgets set log = 'v1' where id in (select n.id from {new: id} n);

trg_widgets.sql: update widgets set log = 'v1' where id in (select n.id from {new: id} n);

statements: create trigger trg_widgets after update on widgets for each row begin update widgets set log = 'hotfix' where id = new.id; end

trg_widgets.sql: update widgets set log = 'v2' where id in (select n.id from {new: id} n);
